title: Stake Super - general discussion thread
body:
O.P.
Hi All,
I've recently commenced a SMSF via Stake Super – I noticed that unfortunately there's not a lot happening over at their FB Community group and they also don't have great documentation on their own site (though I've been advised that they are working to have a central resources hub for prospective & new users).
I've found I've had to email to get answers to some basic-ish stuff and will post up here – if you have any tips, tricks or resources feel free to post them up here as well.
Questions also welcomed – as perhaps a Stake Super user here might be able to provide info.
I'm only a month plus with them but I know some pretty savvy folks here are also members – no complaints so far.
So post up anything you have so we can have here as a resource. :-)

---- replies ----
[User #644468179 postsDaniel PlainviewI drink your milkshake!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
In no particular order at all, just grabbing stuff from my comms with Stake Super:
RE: Needing Certified ID for your transfer from existing Super Fund Manager We arrange the certification of these documents in-house and we also take care of posting these documents to your existing Super Fund Manager to help fast track the rollover process for our customers.
You use the below link to upload your documents for Stake Super to certify: https://stakesmsf.com/id-certification-request/
RE: Arranging to have a Stake Super Staff member call you Schedule via the below link: https://calendly.com/stake-super/
RE: Binding Death Benefit Nomination Request Form Stake Super uses the below link for you to put a binding death benefit nomination in place: https://fs23.formsite. com/TzvDEa/bvxummdmvu/index.html
RE: Sample EOFY reports I queried what they send to clients – was provided with these as a demo of the reports sent out: https://file.io/c8FaCYSM2fTT
RE: Off-market transfers of equities into your SMSF e.g in specie transfers Was advised the following by Stake Super: We also do not charge for any OMTs that would be treated as a contribution to the SMSF. Our team are also happy to assist with the forms at no extra charge.
RE: Notice of Intent forms (where member makes a post-tax contribution and wishes to claim as concessional and receive tax deduction: We also look after the preparation of notice of intent forms in the case where member make personal concessional contributions to the fund in any given financial year.
I'll post a few more up later – have to check through emails – feel free to chuck up what you have.
[User #24515710423 posts~~CbR~~opinion, not adviceWhirlpool Forums Addict] Spoke to Stake SMSF recently as part of considering moving my SMSF over from eSuperFund but the discussion with them was underwhelming for much the same reasons you describe – lack of easily available information (especially compared to how much info eSuperFund had available even back in 2017!) , and the way they present information wasn't comfort inducing.
e.g. – they started off my telling me that any "balance available" within your StakeSMSF Account won't be guaranteed by the Deposit Guarantee as they manage those balances using an internal ledger. Immediate red flags. But what they don't tell you (and should, upfront) is you can open a Macquarie Bank SMSF Account that is covered by the Deposit Guarantee, and can be used to fund (but not settle, as you would, with Commsec) trades via Stake, and indeed have it function as the main bank account for your SMSF (incl depositing your regular employer contributions).

Nick the Knife writes...
PS. I note they seem to now imply that the deposit guarantee scheme does apply to funds in your Stake 'Wallet':
That's not what the quoted text is saying at all. The words "bank guarantee" are doing the heavy lifting there, but what it is saying is that an Australian Bank (not the Australian Government, as is the case with actual bank deposits upto $250,000) is guaranteeing those deposits up to the face value (not at face value, but up to).
More details here https://help.airwallex.com/hc /en-gb/articles/6087666926607
What is a bank guarantee?
A bank guarantee is a guarantee issued by a bank which specifies a beneficiary and a face value. The beneficiary is able to present the bank guarantee to the issuing bank to claim payment up to the face value of the guarantee. In Airwallex’s case, the named beneficiary of the bank guarantee(s) is the independent third-party trustee (GLAS) who holds the guarantee(s) on behalf of you, our customers.
List of financial institutions covered by Australian Government's deposit guarantee scheme here: https://www.apra.gov.au/list- of-authorised-deposit-taking -institutions-covered-under-financial-claims-scheme
and a much straightforward process to recover funds in the event of a bank collapse is here:
https://www.apra.gov.au/freq uently-asked-questions-about -activation-payments-and-adm inistration-of-financial-claims-scheme

PS. It's pretty clear Stake has gone about a convoluted methodology for client accounts – whenever a financial services co does this its generally for their own benefit – the description of how SAFE client funds are seems opaque at best – @andrew99999 stated this when he did a review of Stake's brokerage side (which obviously uses the same Air Wallex 'wallet' for holding client funds:
The AUD Wallet
While the AUD wallet is described as a digital bank account, and which has its own BSB & account number, it is neither a bank account nor is it a separate account from other individuals. The current Airwallex/Stake PDS (as of August 2022) says that “Funds represented by the Wallet will be collected and pooled with funds of other clients of Airwallex in one or more client trust accounts with a licensed bank in Australia.” It also states that “Airwallex is not a bank”. However, as of March 2023, the updated document states that the funds in your Wallet are protected under the Commonwealth guarantee by Global Loan Agency Services Australia Nominees (GLAS) in case Airwallex is found by APRA to be in breach if it’s legal obligation.
The PDS also states “This PDS has not been lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) and is not required to be by the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth)”. This means there is no requirement for disclosure and auditing of accounts.
While the updated addition of the Commonwealth guarantee is a big step in the right direction, my suggestion would be not to keep cash in brokerage trust accounts for long periods and only move money into there when you are ready to trade as soon as it hits the wallet, and when selling, move it out as soon as it is settled. And this would also be my recommendation with other brokers.
https://passiveinvestingaustralia.com/stake-review/

[User #24515710423 posts~~CbR~~opinion, not adviceWhirlpool Forums Addict] Nick the Knife writes...
but you see this as a big difference to the point of being a problem?
In an of itself it'd be less of a problem. The fact that they've gone about using the terms that can reasonably confuse (as it did, you) the nature of guarantee is just clumsy.
Let us assume that a proactive trustee would leave the funds in their wallet for as short a duration as possible. At the same time, unless there is an actual bank account in which your employer pays your Super, there will be a non-trivial amount collecting in the wallet at any point in time.
If you could explain this further that would be appreciated.
The way I see it, if your SMSF holds an account with the bank and the bank goes under, your deposit is covered upto $250k as long as the bank in question is an Authorised Deposit Taking Institution, and APRA steps in to make you whole under a known and published process.
If your SMSF places money in an Airwallex Wallet and Airwallex (or Stake) goes under, you are essentially a creditor to the relevant business, and you are left chasing (via GLAS) the monies along with every other creditor, and aren't guaranteed to get 100 cents on the dollar.
I'm not sure (and so, I could be entirely wrong) how Stake/Airwallex claims the funds are protected under Commonwealth Guarantee by GLAS given: a) the APRA website clearly lists the financial institutions covered by the guarantee b) the Guarantee only applies to balances upto $250,000
Furthermore, APRA clearly lists who qualifies as an account holder to benefit from this guarantee
https://www.apra.gov.au/freq uently-asked-questions-about -banking-and-financial-claims-scheme
If Airwallex is operating a ledger with a sole underlying account (or less underlying accounts than available ledgers) then it is entirely possible that the ledger balance would be higher than what is covered by the Guarantee, unless they're somehow tracking the ledgers to underlying account mapping and creating new accounts to stay under the $250k guarantee threshold – at which point it all seems far to complex for not much gain from Stake's perspective when having 1:1 accounts per SMSF would be far simpler and cleaner.

I'll report back what Stake SUper say – thank you again for your constructive feedback – thats kind of the idea for the thread so great job!
